story.title: Avalanche on Broad Peak Leaves Renowned Climber Missing and Four Bodies Found
story.summary: An avalanche on Broad Peak in northern Pakistan has left ten climbers missing, including renowned mountaineer Nirmal Purja. Rescue teams have recovered four bodies from the site while continuing their search for the remaining climbers despite challenging weather conditions.

explore_lenses.label: Why is the rescue so difficult?
explore_lenses.title: Weather and terrain constrain access
explore_lenses.summary: The search is taking place on an 8,000-meter peak in the Karakoram, where the missing team has had no contact with base camp since the avalanche. Pakistani officials say poor weather has limited helicopter operations, while the remaining search area is remote and difficult.

claims.text: Broad Peak is about 8,047-8,051 meters high and is the world’s 12th-highest mountain, placing the incident in extreme high-altitude terrain.
Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain said adverse weather was hampering the rescue, and the Alpine Club of Pakistan said helicopter support depended on weather and operational conditions.
Gilgit-Baltistan tourism official Sajid Hussain told Reuters that the search for the six people not yet located was focused on a remote, difficult area.
The Alpine Club of Pakistan says the team has been out of communication since the avalanche, limiting confirmed information about survivors’ locations and condition.

explore_lenses.label: Who was on Nirmal Purja’s expedition?
explore_lenses.title: A multinational team led by a record climber
explore_lenses.summary: The incident involves a multinational party led by Nirmal Purja, a Nepal-born British mountaineer whose 2019 ascent of all 14 eight-thousanders brought global attention to his work. The identities and nationalities in early official accounts are not fully consistent.

claims.text: The Alpine Club of Pakistan identified Purja as the expedition leader and said the 10-person party included five Nepali climbers, Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, Omani climber Nathira, American climber Mallory Geis, a Chinese climber identified as Wang, and one other foreign climber.
Purja climbed all 14 peaks above 8,000 meters in six months and six days in 2019, a then-record achievement; he also helped complete the first winter ascent of K2 in 2021.
China’s Foreign Ministry said on July 31 that it was urgently verifying whether a Chinese national was among those missing and was willing to assist Pakistan if needed.

Early accounts differ on the party’s foreign nationals: the Alpine Club’s roster cited an American and a Chinese climber, while police reporting cited two British nationals; this has not been reconciled publicly.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next in the search?
explore_lenses.title: Recovery and search operations continue
explore_lenses.summary: Rescuers have located four bodies and are continuing to look for the other six missing climbers. The immediate next steps depend on whether weather permits teams and helicopters to reach, recover and identify those located.

claims.text: Rescuers located four bodies on July 31 and continued searching for the other six climbers, according to Pakistani officials cited by AP.
The Alpine Club of Pakistan said it was mobilizing helicopter support and all available rescue resources, subject to weather and operational conditions.

Forecast: Search and recovery efforts are expected to continue when operational conditions allow, based on the Alpine Club’s stated mobilization of rescue resources and officials’ confirmation that the search was ongoing.

Two bodies were identified by the Alpine Club as Omani climber Nadhira Al Harthy and Nepali climber Pur Bahadur Gurung, but other reporting said authorities had not identified the bodies; official identification remains incomplete.

story_report.summary: An avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan has left 10 climbers missing, including expedition leader Nirmal Purja, while rescue teams have recovered four bodies. The search is continuing in extreme high-altitude terrain, but adverse weather and the party’s loss of communication have limited rescue operations and information about survivors.

sections.heading: Broad Peak Rescue Conditions
sections.body: Broad Peak rises about 8,047 to 8,051 meters and is the world’s 12th-highest mountain. Gilgit-Baltistan Chief Minister Amjad Hussain said adverse weather was hampering the rescue, while the Alpine Club of Pakistan said helicopter support depended on weather and operational conditions. Tourism official Sajid Hussain said the search for six people not yet located was focused on a remote, difficult area.

sections.heading: Purja and Expedition Party
sections.body: The Alpine Club of Pakistan identified Purja as the expedition leader. Its roster said the 10-person party included five Nepali climbers, Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, Omani climber Nathira, American climber Mallory Geis, a Chinese climber identified as Wang and another foreign climber. Purja climbed all 14 peaks above 8,000 meters in six months and six days in 2019, a then-record achievement, and helped complete the first winter ascent of K2 in 2021.

sections.heading: Search and Identification Effort
sections.body: Pakistani officials said rescuers located four bodies on July 31 and continued searching for the other six climbers. The Alpine Club said it was mobilizing helicopter support and all available rescue resources, subject to conditions. The club identified two of the bodies as Omani climber Nadhira Al Harthy and Nepali climber Pur Bahadur Gurung, though other reporting said authorities had not identified the bodies.

related_stories.title: Rescue Efforts Ongoing After Fatal Coal Mine Explosion in Pakistan
related_stories.summary: A coal mine explosion in Balochistan, Pakistan, has resulted in the deaths of at least 34 workers, with two miners still unaccounted for. The blast, attributed to a buildup of methane gas, also affected two nearby mines. Rescue operations are currently underway as authorities continue to search for the missing miners.

related_stories.summary: Franco Baresi, a legendary defender for AC Milan and the Italian national team, has died at the age of 66. Baresi was celebrated for his contributions to football during the 1980s and 1990s, including winning the World Cup with Italy.

related_stories.title: Trump Indicates No Objection to Withdrawing Todd Blanche's Nomination Amid Senate Delays
related_stories.summary: President Donald Trump has stated he has 'no objection' to withdrawing Todd Blanche's nomination for Attorney General. This comes as two Republican senators, Thom Tillis and John Cornyn, are withholding support, leading to a delay in the Senate vote. The senators are seeking a written commitment from the Department of Justice regarding a disputed compensation fund that could benefit Trump allies.
